questions.stem:
A firm has signed a B101-2017 agreement for a new two-story branch library with a small cafe. The agreement adds landscape design as a supplemental service. The owner will provide the boundary and topographic survey and the geotechnical report, and the site is a former parking lot with no known contamination.

Which consultants should the architect engage?

options.explanation: Correct. Structural engineering is part of the architect's basic services.
Correct. MEP engineering is part of the architect's basic services.
Correct. The agreement adds landscape design as a supplemental service, so the architect provides it.
The owner provides the geotechnical report under B101-2017 Art. 5.
The owner provides the survey.
Testing is an owner responsibility, and nothing suggests contamination.

questions.explanation: Read the agreement: basic + supplemental services define the architect's consultants; Art. 5 defines the owner's.
questions.confidenceNote: Paragraph number per my knowledge of the AIA document; confirm against your copy (free via your NCARB Record).

questions.stem:
An architect is selecting a structural engineer for a four-story hospital addition in a high-seismic region. The prime agreement requires each consultant to carry professional liability insurance of $2,000,000 per claim. Three firms have submitted proposals, and the hospital's schedule requires construction documents in nine months.

Which criteria should drive the selection?

options.explanation: Correct. Building-type and seismic experience bear directly on quality and risk.
Correct. The engineer must be licensed where the project is located.

options.text: Professional liability coverage that meets the prime agreement
options.explanation: Correct. Consultant coverage must match what the architect promised the owner.

options.text: The lowest fee among the three proposals
options.explanation: Fee matters, but choosing on fee alone risks quality and coordination problems.

options.text: The office closest to the architect's office
options.explanation: Proximity to the architect is secondary to expertise and licensure.

options.text: The largest firm by number of employees
options.explanation: Size doesn't guarantee relevant expertise or availability.

questions.explanation: Select consultants on expertise, licensure, capacity and insurance, then fee.

questions.stem:
At the kickoff meeting for a 90,000 sf office building, the project manager wants to settle responsibilities within the architect's team before production starts. The team includes a principal, a project architect, two designers, a specification writer and a construction administration specialist.

Which responsibilities should be assigned at the kickoff?

options.explanation: Correct. One person must own consultant coordination.

options.text: Performing and updating the code analysis
options.explanation: Correct. Code compliance needs a clear owner from the start.
Correct. Someone must document decisions and distribute them.
Correct. Assigning CA duties early lets that person follow the design.
The owner and contractor sign their own agreement. The architect isn't a party.

options.text: Setting the contractor's means and methods
options.explanation: Means and methods are the contractor's responsibility (A201-2017 §3.3.1).

questions.explanation: Define internal roles early: coordination, code, communication, CA.

questions.stem:
On a new community recreation center, the architect has engaged structural, MEP, civil and landscape consultants. Before design development, the project manager prepares a responsibility matrix, because items that fall between disciplines caused change orders on the firm's last project.

Which items commonly fall between disciplines and should be assigned explicitly?

options.explanation: Correct. It's often unclear whether electrical or landscape owns it.
Correct. Civil and plumbing scopes often overlap at the building line.
Correct. It may fall to electrical, a fire-protection engineer, or the contractor's design-build scope.
Roof framing clearly belongs to the structural engineer.
Ductwork clearly belongs to the mechanical engineer.
Floor plans clearly belong to the architect.

questions.explanation: A responsibility matrix closes scope gaps before they become change orders.

questions.stem:
A firm's total fee for a medical office building is $640,000. The firm has agreed to these consultant fees:

- Structural engineer: 9% of the total fee
- MEP engineer: 18% of the total fee
- Civil engineer: fixed fee of $24,000

How much of the fee remains for the architect's own services?

options.explanation: This applies the percentages after subtracting the civil fee. They're percentages of the total fee.
This leaves out the civil engineer's fixed fee.
This leaves out the MEP engineer's fee.

questions.stem:
A project manager is staffing design development for a clinic. The phase fee for the architect's own services is $120,000, and the firm uses a blended billing rate of $150 per hour. The project architect will work 25 hours per week on the project for the 10-week phase.

How many hours remain for the rest of the team?

options.explanation: That's the project architect's hours, not the remainder.
Correct. The fee supports 800 hours, and the project architect uses 250.
That's the total hours the fee supports, before the project architect's time.
This adds the project architect's hours instead of subtracting them.

questions.stem:
Construction documents for a school are estimated at 3,600 hours of work over 12 weeks. Because of other commitments and non-billable time, each staff member assigned can give the project about 32 hours per week.

How many staff should the project manager plan to assign?

options.explanation: This assumes 40 hours per week from each person.
This rounds 9.4 down, which leaves the work short of hours.
Correct. 3,600 ÷ (12 × 32) = 9.4, which rounds up to 10 people.

questions.explanation:
1. Hours per person = 12 weeks × 32 = 384
2. Staff needed = 3,600 ÷ 384 = 9.4 → 10

questions.stem:
Midway through design, the owner asks the architect to add an acoustical consultant for a new performance hall. The agreement provides that added consultants are billed at their fee times 1.10, plus the architect's coordination time at hourly rates.

- Acoustical consultant's proposal: $18,000
- Architect's coordination: 20 hours at $140

What should the architect propose for this additional service?

options.explanation: This passes the consultant's fee through without the markup or coordination time.
This leaves out the architect's coordination time.
This leaves out the 1.10 markup on the consultant's fee.

questions.stem:
A firm assigns an experienced but unlicensed project architect to lead production for a warehouse. The firm's only licensed architect is a principal who works on several projects. The client asks who will be responsible for the sealed documents.

Which arrangement meets professional requirements?

options.text: The project architect seals the documents as production lead.
options.explanation: An unlicensed person can't seal documents.

options.text: The licensed principal directs the work and seals it.
options.explanation: Correct. A licensed architect must exercise responsible control over the work they seal (NCARB 5.1).

options.text: The structural engineer seals the architectural drawings.
options.explanation: Engineers seal their own discipline's work, not the architectural documents.

options.text: The principal seals the documents after a final review only.
options.explanation: Responsible control requires direction and supervision during the work, not a review at the end.

questions.explanation: Responsible control: a licensed architect directs, supervises, and seals.

flashcards.back: The scope in the owner–architect agreement: basic + supplemental services, delivery method, schedule and fee.
Structural, mechanical and electrical engineering (§3.1). Others only if added as supplemental services.

flashcards.back: Building-type experience, licensure, capacity, coordination record, insurance matching the prime agreement, and fee, never fee alone.
C401-2017, which mirrors prime-agreement duties and insurance.
Assigns items that span disciplines (site lighting, stormwater, fire alarm, low voltage) to prevent gaps and overlaps.
A licensed architect directs and supervises the work, and seals only that work (NCARB 5.1).
The architect's fee normally includes its consultants' fees. Get consultant proposals before setting your fee.
An additional service: the consultant's fee × the agreed markup, plus the architect's coordination time.
Hours ÷ (weeks × hours each person can give per week), rounded up.
Principal-in-charge, project manager, project architect, designers, spec writer/QC reviewer, CA staff.
